title: VLSM planning
summary: Give each network the size it needs, from one block, without overlaps or waste.

steps.title: Different sizes from one block
body: Equal subnets waste space: a two-router link doesn't need 62 addresses. **VLSM** (variable length subnet masking) gives each network its own prefix.
Plan `192.168.10.0/24` for LAN A (100 hosts), LAN B (50), LAN C (20) and two router links (2 each). **Largest first**:

lines: List every network and its host count
Sort them from largest to smallest
Pick the smallest subnet that fits each
Allocate each at the next free address
also: List every network and its host count
Pick the smallest subnet that fits each
Sort them from largest to smallest
Allocate each at the next free address
steps.explain: Sorting first guarantees every allocation lands on a correct boundary.

steps.prompt: Continue the plan above with LAN D (10 hosts) in the free space.
steps.explain: 10 hosts need a /28 (14 usable). The next free address .232 isn't a multiple of 16, so it goes at .240; .232/29 stays free.

steps.title: Alignment
body: A subnet must **start on a multiple of its own size**. A /26 (64 addresses) can start at .0, .64, .128 or .192, never at .32.
Allocating largest first keeps this automatic. Allocate small ones first and you'll leave holes the big ones can't use.

steps.prompt: A plan gives LAN X `10.5.0.0/23` and LAN Y `10.5.1.0/24`. What's wrong?
steps.explain: A /23 covers two /24s. Overlaps cause hosts in one LAN to be unreachable from the other.

steps.title: Overlap check
prompt: Write `bool Overlaps(string a, string b)`: two CIDR blocks overlap when one contains the other's network, i.e. they agree on the bits of the **shorter** prefix.
starter: uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);

hints: Mask both with the smaller prefix.

steps.title: VLSM planner
prompt: Write `List<string> Vlsm(string block, List<(string Name, int Hosts)> needs)` returning `"{Name} {network}/{prefix}"` lines in allocation order:

largest host count first (keep input order for ties), each given the smallest subnet that fits (the longest prefix up to /30, as `PrefixForHosts` from *Subnetting a block* returns: paste or rewrite it), allocated back to back from the block's start.

template: var dojoPlan = Vlsm("192.168.10.0/24", new List<(string Name, int Hosts)> { ("Link1", 2), ("C", 20), ("A", 100), ("Link2", 2), ("B", 50) });
Dojo.Eq("bigger block", new List<string> { "HQ 10.20.0.0/23", "Branch 10.20.2.0/24" }, Vlsm("10.20.0.0/22", new List<(string Name, int Hosts)> { ("Branch", 200), ("HQ", 500) }));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("doesn't fit", () => Vlsm("192.168.10.0/24", new List<(string Name, int Hosts)> { ("A", 200), ("B", 100) }));
hints: `OrderByDescending` is stable, so ties keep input order.
